outline: Diabetes mellitus and other disorders of the endocrine pancreas
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: A glucagon-secreting pancreatic alpha-cell neuroendocrine tumor causes sustained glucagon-receptor signaling. In hepatocytes, glucagon activates a Gs-coupled receptor, increasing adenylyl cyclase activity and cAMP, which promotes hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Hyperglucagonemia produces hyperglycemia and a catabolic state; necrolytic migratory erythema is a characteristic associated dermatosis.
vignette: A 58-year-old woman has several months of progressive weight loss, new hyperglycemia, and recurrent painful erythematous, scaly plaques involving the groin, lower abdomen, and distal extremities. The lesions appear in crops and are present at different stages of healing. Abdominal imaging shows a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
lead: Which physiologic effect is most likely caused by the hormone secreted by this tumor?
correct: Increased hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis through cAMP signaling
distractors: Increased skeletal muscle and adipose glucose uptake through insulin receptor tyrosine kinase signaling
Increased intestinal water and electrolyte secretion through VPAC receptor cAMP signaling
Increased gastric acid secretion through CCK-B receptor signaling
Suppression of insulin secretion and gallbladder emptying by excess somatostatin
distractor_notes: Insulin acts through a receptor tyrosine kinase and promotes GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue while opposing hepatic glucose production. That physiology is associated with insulin, not glucagon excess.

VIP activates VPAC G-protein-coupled receptors and raises intestinal cAMP, increasing water, electrolyte, and bicarbonate secretion; this produces the secretory-diarrhea phenotype of VIPoma rather than necrolytic migratory erythema with hyperglycemia.

Gastrin activates CCK-B receptors on parietal and enterochromaffin-like cells, increasing gastric acid secretion. Gastrinoma therefore causes acid-peptic disease rather than the glucagonoma syndrome shown here.

Somatostatin excess suppresses insulin secretion and decreases cholecystokinin release/gallbladder emptying, contributing to diabetes, steatorrhea, and cholelithiasis in somatostatinoma. The characteristic necrolytic migratory erythema in this vignette instead points to glucagon excess.
key_expl: The combination of new hyperglycemia, progressive weight loss, a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, and necrolytic migratory erythema identifies glucagonoma syndrome. Glucagon binds a Gs-coupled receptor on hepatocytes, activates adenylyl cyclase, and raises cAMP. The resulting signaling increases hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, driving hyperglycemia and contributing to the catabolic phenotype.
objective: Recognize glucagonoma from necrolytic migratory erythema, weight loss, and hyperglycemia, and connect glucagon excess to Gs-cAMP-mediated hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
